capital.zh: 汤加塔布岛穆阿（拉帕哈）

summary.en: The sacred paramount line of Tonga, traced in oral tradition to ʻAhoʻeitu in the 10th century. From the royal centre at Muʻa its chiefs drew tribute and marriage ties from Samoa, ʻUvea, Fiji and beyond. Political power later passed to the Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua and Tuʻi Kanokupolu lines; the title lapsed in 1865.
summary.zh: 汤加神圣的最高酋长世系，口述传统追溯至10世纪的阿霍艾伊图。其酋长以汤加塔布岛穆阿为王都，从萨摩亚、瓦利斯、斐济等地获得贡品并结成联姻网络。实权后来转入图伊哈阿塔卡劳阿与图伊卡诺库波卢两系，1865年该称号终止。

name.zh: 阿霍艾伊图（传说中的开创者）
劳菲利汤加（末代图伊汤加）

sources.title: Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: Tongans
E. Bott, Tongan Society at the Time of Captain Cook's Visits (Polynesian Society, 1982)
G. Clark, D. Burley & T. Murray, 'Monumentality and the development of the Tongan maritime chiefdom', Antiquity 82 (2008)

note: Early reign dates are generational estimates from royal genealogies; the term 'empire' is contested by archaeologists, who prefer 'maritime chiefdom'. Tuʻitātui's and Talakaifaiki's dates are approximate.

story.en:
Tongan tradition says the first Tuʻi Tonga, ʻAhoʻeitu, was the son of the sky god Tangaloa ʻEitumatupuʻa and a woman of Tongatapu. His descendants were sacred: commoners could not touch them, and each year the first fruits of the land were presented to them at the ʻinasi ceremony.

From about the 12th century the line built in stone. Tuʻitātui is credited with the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui trilithon, and the royal centre at Muʻa grew a harbour and terraced tombs, the langi. Archaeologists see a maritime chiefdom whose double-hulled canoes linked Tongatapu with Samoa, ʻUvea, Futuna and Fiji by tribute, marriage and war. Samoan tradition remembers driving the Tongans out under Talakaifaiki, the origin of the Malietoa title.

After the assassination of Takalauʻa in the 15th century, his son delegated government to a new secular line, the Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua, which in turn created the Tuʻi Kanokupolu. The sacred title survived until Laufilitonga died in 1865, by which time Tāufaʻāhau (George Tupou I) ruled all Tonga.
story.zh:
汤加传说称，首位图伊汤加阿霍艾伊图是天神坦加罗阿·埃伊图马图普阿与汤加塔布岛一名女子之子。他的后裔神圣不可侵犯：平民不得触碰，每年土地上的初熟果实都要在“伊纳西”仪式上献给他们。

约自12世纪起，这一世系开始兴建石构建筑。哈阿蒙加毛伊三石门传为图伊塔图伊所建，王都穆阿则发展出港口和称为“朗伊”的阶梯式王陵。考古学者认为这是一个海上酋邦：双体独木舟通过贡赋、联姻和战争把汤加塔布与萨摩亚、瓦利斯、富图纳和斐济联系在一起。萨摩亚传统则记得在塔拉凯法伊基时代把汤加人逐出萨摩亚，这被视为“马列托阿”称号的由来。

15世纪塔卡劳阿遇刺后，其子把世俗政务交给新设的图伊哈阿塔卡劳阿一系，后者又分出图伊卡诺库波卢一系。神圣称号一直延续到1865年劳菲利汤加去世，那时陶法阿豪（乔治·图普一世）已统治全汤加。

summary.en: The first centralised government of Pohnpei in the Caroline Islands, ruling from the basalt islet city of Nan Madol. Oral tradition remembers its lords as increasingly oppressive until the Kosraean hero Isokelekel overthrew the last Saudeleur and founded the Nahnmwarki chiefly system that survives today.
summary.zh: 加罗林群岛波纳佩岛上第一个中央集权政权，以玄武岩人工岛城南马都尔为都。口述传统记载其统治者日益暴虐，最终科斯雷英雄伊索克雷克尔推翻末代绍德雷尔，建立延续至今的“南姆瓦尔基”酋长制度。

name.zh: 奥洛索帕（传说中的开创者）
绍德姆沃尔（末代绍德雷尔）

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Nan Madol: Ceremonial Centre of Eastern Micronesia
D. Hanlon, Upon a Stone Altar: A History of the Island of Pohnpei to 1890 (University of Hawaii Press, 1988)

note: Ruler names come from Pohnpeian oral history; the regnal dates are placeholders spread across a dynasty archaeologically dated c. 1100/1200–c. 1628.

story.en:
Pohnpeian tradition tells of two brothers, the sorcerers Olisihpa and Olosohpa, who came by canoe from the west looking for a place to build an altar. After several failed attempts they settled on the reef off Temwen Island, where their magic flew the great basalt columns into place. When Olisihpa died, Olosohpa became the first Saudeleur, 'lord of Deleur'.

His successors centralised the island: commoners owed tribute in food, fish and labour, and the lords lived among the priests and tombs of Nan Madol. Over the generations, the stories say, their demands grew more tyrannical and their offence against the thunder god Nahnsapwe more grievous.

Nahnsapwe's son Isokelekel sailed from Kosrae with 333 followers, according to the oral account, and defeated the last Saudeleur, Saudemwohl, who fled and turned into a fish in a stream. Isokelekel took the title Nahnmwarki. Archaeology dates this transition to about 1628, and Nan Madol was gradually abandoned afterwards.
story.zh:
波纳佩传统讲述了两位巫师兄弟奥利西帕和奥洛索帕，他们乘独木舟从西方来寻找建造祭坛之地。几经失败后，他们选定了滕文岛外的珊瑚礁，用法术让巨大的玄武岩石柱飞到位置上。奥利西帕去世后，奥洛索帕成为第一位“绍德雷尔”，意为“德雷尔之主”。

他的继任者把全岛置于中央统治之下：平民须以食物、鱼和劳役纳贡，统治者则与祭司和陵墓一同住在南马都尔。传说称，随着世代更替，他们的索取日益暴虐，对雷神南萨普韦的冒犯也愈发严重。

据口述传统，南萨普韦之子伊索克雷克尔率333名追随者从科斯雷渡海而来，击败末代绍德雷尔绍德姆沃尔，后者逃入溪中化为一条鱼。伊索克雷克尔取得“南姆瓦尔基”称号。考古学将这一转变定在约1628年，此后南马都尔逐渐被废弃。

summary.en: The paramount chiefdom (aupuni) of Hawaiʻi Island, one of several rival island kingdoms before unification. ʻUmi-a-Līloa is remembered as uniting the island's districts around 1500; his descendants, through Keawe, Alapaʻinui and Kalaniʻōpuʻu, ruled until Kamehameha I won the island and then the archipelago.
summary.zh: 夏威夷岛的最高酋邦，是统一前几个相互竞争的岛国之一。传统认为乌米·阿·利洛阿约在1500年统一了岛上各区；他的后裔经凯阿韦、阿拉帕伊努伊和卡拉尼奥普乌一路统治，直到卡美哈梅哈一世夺取全岛并进而统一群岛。

name.zh: 凯阿韦伊克卡希阿利伊奥卡莫库

sources.title: S. M. Kamakau, Ruling Chiefs of Hawaii (Kamehameha Schools Press, rev. ed. 1992)
P. V. Kirch, How Chiefs Became Kings: Divine Kingship and the Rise of Archaic States in Ancient Hawaiʻi (University of California Press, 2010)

note: Reigns before the late 18th century are genealogical estimates (about 20–25 years per generation); Kamehameha controlled the island in stages between 1782 and 1791.

summary.en: Founded when Kamehameha I conquered Oʻahu in 1795 and completed in 1810 when Kauaʻi submitted, the kingdom became an internationally recognised constitutional monarchy with treaties, a legislature and near-universal literacy. American-backed businessmen overthrew Queen Liliʻuokalani in 1893.
summary.zh: 1795年卡美哈梅哈一世征服瓦胡岛而建立王国，1810年考艾岛归附后完成统一。王国发展为受国际承认的君主立宪国家，拥有条约、议会和近乎普及的识字率。1893年，美国支持的商人推翻了利留卡拉尼女王。

name.zh: 卡美哈梅哈二世（利霍利霍）
卡美哈梅哈三世（考伊克奥乌利）

sources.title: R. S. Kuykendall, The Hawaiian Kingdom, 3 vols. (University of Hawaii Press, 1938–1967)

note: Some reckonings start the kingdom in 1782 (Kamehameha's rise on Hawaiʻi Island) or 1810 (Kauaʻi's submission); 1795, the conquest of Oʻahu, follows Kuykendall.

story.en:
After the battle of Nuʻuanu in 1795 Kamehameha held every island except Kauaʻi, whose king Kaumualiʻi accepted his overlordship peacefully in 1810. Kamehameha governed through trusted chiefs and profited from the sandalwood trade with China; when he died in 1819 his widow Kaʻahumanu became kuhina nui (co-ruler) and helped end the kapu system.

Under Kamehameha III the kingdom remade itself as a modern state: a declaration of rights in 1839, a written constitution in 1840, the Māhele land division of 1848, and recognition of independence by Britain and France in 1843. Hawaiian-language newspapers flourished, and literacy rates rivalled any in the world.

Yet disease cut the Native Hawaiian population from several hundred thousand to about 40,000 by the 1890s, while sugar planters of American descent gained economic power. In 1887 they forced King Kalākaua to sign the 'Bayonet Constitution'; in 1893, with US Marines ashore, they deposed his sister Liliʻuokalani.
story.zh:
1795年努乌阿努战役后，卡美哈梅哈已控制除考艾岛以外的所有岛屿；1810年考艾国王考穆阿利伊和平接受其宗主权。卡美哈梅哈通过亲信酋长治理，并从对华檀香木贸易中获利；1819年他去世后，遗孀卡阿胡马努出任“库希纳努伊”（共治者），并推动废除了禁忌制度。

卡美哈梅哈三世在位时，王国改造为现代国家：1839年颁布权利宣言，1840年制定成文宪法，1848年进行“大分地”，1843年英法承认其独立。夏威夷语报纸兴盛，识字率堪比世界任何地方。

然而疾病使夏威夷原住民人口从数十万降至19世纪90年代的约四万，美裔甘蔗种植园主则掌握了经济权力。1887年他们迫使卡拉卡瓦国王签署“刺刀宪法”；1893年，在美国海军陆战队登岸的情况下，他们废黜了卡拉卡瓦之妹利留卡拉尼。

summary.en: The Pōmare family, allied with European sailors and missionaries, unified Tahiti and neighbouring islands into a kingdom that adopted Protestant Christianity and a written law code in 1819. France imposed a protectorate in 1842 and annexed the kingdom when Pōmare V ceded it in 1880.
summary.zh: 波马雷家族借助欧洲水手与传教士的支持，统一了塔希提及邻近岛屿，王国接受新教并于1819年颁布成文法典。法国于1842年强行建立保护国，1880年波马雷五世让出王国，法国随即将其吞并。

sources.title: C. Newbury, Tahiti Nui: Change and Survival in French Polynesia 1767–1945 (University of Hawaii Press, 1980)

note: Pōmare I formally passed the title to his son in 1791 but remained the real power until his death in 1803; Pōmare II's supremacy was secured only at the battle of Te Feipī in 1815.

story.en:
When European ships began calling at Matavai Bay in the late 1760s, Tahiti was divided among rival chiefly districts. The chief Tū of Pare, later known as Pōmare I, used the muskets and help of visiting sailors, including some of the Bounty mutineers, to raise his family above the others, although Tahitians did not regard him as a king in the European sense.

His son Pōmare II lost power in 1808 and fled to Moʻorea, where he turned to the missionaries of the London Missionary Society. After his victory at Te Feipī in 1815 he ruled Tahiti as a Christian king, destroying the marae of ʻOro and issuing a written law code in 1819. Mission presses and schools turned Tahitian into a written language.

Independence did not last. Queen Pōmare IV's expulsion of two French Catholic priests in 1836 gave France a pretext; Admiral Dupetit-Thouars imposed a protectorate in 1842, and after the Franco-Tahitian War the queen accepted it in 1847. Her son Pōmare V ceded his realm to France in 1880, and Tahiti became part of the French Establishments in Oceania, later French Polynesia.
story.zh:
18世纪60年代末欧洲船只开始停靠马塔瓦伊湾时，塔希提分属彼此竞争的各酋长辖区。帕雷的酋长图（后称波马雷一世）借助来访水手（包括部分“邦蒂号”叛变者）的火枪和帮助，使自己的家族凌驾于其他家族之上，不过塔希提人并不把他视为欧洲意义上的国王。

其子波马雷二世于1808年失势，逃往莫雷阿岛，在那里转而依靠伦敦传道会的传教士。1815年特费皮之战获胜后，他以基督徒国王的身份统治塔希提，摧毁奥罗神的马拉埃，并于1819年颁布成文法典。传教团的印刷所和学校使塔希提语成为书面语言。

王国的独立未能长久。1836年波马雷四世女王驱逐两名法国天主教神父，给了法国干涉的借口；1842年迪佩蒂-图阿尔海军上将强行建立保护国，法塔战争后女王于1847年接受保护。1880年其子波马雷五世把王国让与法国，塔希提并入法属大洋洲殖民地，即后来的法属波利尼西亚。

summary.en: Tāufaʻāhau, the Tuʻi Kanokupolu, became paramount in 1845, united Tonga by 1852 and reigned as George Tupou I. His 1875 constitution, emancipation of commoners and land law shaped the only Pacific kingdom never formally colonised; it was a British protected state from 1900 to 1970.
summary.zh: 图伊卡诺库波卢陶法阿豪1845年成为最高首领，至1852年统一汤加，称乔治·图普一世。他1875年颁布的宪法、解放平民的法令和土地法，塑造了太平洋上唯一从未被正式殖民的王国；1900至1970年汤加为英国保护国。

sources.title: I. C. Campbell, Island Kingdom: Tonga Ancient and Modern (Canterbury University Press, 2nd ed. 2001)

story.en:
Tonga's modern kingdom was built by Tāufaʻāhau, a chief of Haʻapai who adopted Methodism in 1831 and took the baptismal name Siaosi (George). Using Christian allies as well as war, he overcame rival chiefs on Vavaʻu and Tongatapu and in 1845 became Tuʻi Kanokupolu; by 1852, when the last independent chiefs fell, he ruled all Tonga.

Determined to keep the islands out of European hands, George Tupou I issued written law codes in 1839 and 1850, freed commoners from forced labour for the chiefs in 1862, and in 1875 granted a constitution, drafted with the missionary Shirley Baker. It created a parliament, guaranteed basic freedoms and forbade the sale of land, which was to be held under the Crown and allotted to Tongans.

In 1900 his great-grandson George Tupou II signed a treaty of friendship that made Tonga a British protected state while it kept its own king and government. Queen Sālote guided it through much of the 20th century, and full control of foreign affairs returned in 1970. A democracy movement, and riots in Nukuʻalofa in 2006, led to the reforms of 2010, under which the people elect most members of parliament; the monarchy remains central under King Tupou VI.
story.zh:
汤加的近代王国由陶法阿豪缔造。他是哈派群岛的酋长，1831年皈依卫理宗，取教名“西奥西”（乔治）。他既依靠基督教盟友，也诉诸战争，先后战胜瓦瓦乌和汤加塔布的对手，1845年成为图伊卡诺库波卢；到1852年最后一批独立酋长落败，他才统治全汤加。

为使群岛不落入欧洲人之手，乔治·图普一世于1839年和1850年颁布成文法典，1862年解除平民为酋长服劳役的义务，1875年在传教士雪利·贝克协助下颁布宪法。宪法设立议会，保障基本自由，并禁止出售土地，土地归王室所有，分配给汤加人使用。

1900年，他的曾孙乔治·图普二世签订友好条约，使汤加成为英国保护国，但保留本国国王和政府。萨洛特女王在20世纪大部分时间里领导国家，1970年汤加完全收回外交权。民主运动以及2006年努库阿洛法骚乱促成了2010年的改革，此后议会多数议员由民众选举产生；在图普六世国王治下，君主制仍居核心地位。

summary.en: A short-lived constitutional monarchy proclaimed at Levuka in 1871 under Seru Epenisa Cakobau, Vunivalu of Bau, with a cabinet dominated by European settlers. Bankrupt, divided and unable to control planters or rival chiefs, it ended when Cakobau and leading chiefs ceded Fiji to Britain in October 1874.
summary.zh: 1871年在莱武卡宣布成立的短命君主立宪国，以包岛的武尼瓦卢塞鲁·埃佩尼萨·萨空鲍为国王，内阁由欧洲移民主导。王国财政破产、内部分裂，无力约束种植园主和敌对酋长，1874年10月萨空鲍与主要酋长将斐济割让给英国，王国告终。

sources.title: D. Scarr, Fiji: A Short History (Allen & Unwin, 1984)

story.en:
By the end of 1870 some 2,500 Europeans lived in Fiji, many of them cotton planters drawn by the high prices of the American Civil War, but there was no government able to settle land disputes or control the labour trade. Rival chiefs, above all Cakobau of Bau and the Tongan noble Maʻafu in Lau, contended for paramountcy.

In June 1871 a group of settlers persuaded Cakobau to head a constitutional monarchy at Levuka, with a legislature and a cabinet dominated by Europeans such as John Bates Thurston. The Kingdom of Fiji levied taxes, raised a small army and tried to extend its rule into the interior, but planters resented paying, the hill peoples of Viti Levu resisted, and the government's debts mounted.

With cotton prices collapsing, and missionaries and the Australian colonies pressing Britain to stop abuses in the labour trade, Cakobau and the leading chiefs offered the islands to Queen Victoria. Sir Hercules Robinson, governor of New South Wales, negotiated the terms, and on 10 October 1874 the Deed of Cession signed at Levuka ended the kingdom after three years.
story.zh:
到1870年底，斐济已有约2500名欧洲人，其中许多是被美国内战期间棉价高涨吸引而来的棉花种植园主，但当地没有一个能够解决土地纠纷或管控劳工贸易的政府。各酋长，尤其是包岛的萨空鲍和劳群岛的汤加贵族马阿夫，彼此争夺最高地位。

1871年6月，一批移民说服萨空鲍在莱武卡出任君主立宪国的国王，设立立法机构和由约翰·贝茨·瑟斯顿等欧洲人主导的内阁。斐济王国征税、组建小规模军队，并试图把统治扩展到内陆，但种植园主不愿纳税，维提岛山区各族群奋起抵抗，政府债务日益累积。

随着棉价暴跌，加上传教士和澳大利亚各殖民地敦促英国制止劳工贸易中的暴行，萨空鲍与主要酋长把群岛献给维多利亚女王。新南威尔士总督赫拉克勒斯·罗宾逊爵士谈定条件，1874年10月10日在莱武卡签署的《割让契约》结束了这个仅存三年的王国。

summary.en: British Crown colony created by the Deed of Cession of 1874. Governor Arthur Gordon ruled through Fijian chiefs, protected most land as inalienable Fijian property and brought indentured labourers from India, shaping the colony's two-community society until independence in 1970.
summary.zh: 根据1874年《割让契约》建立的英国直辖殖民地。总督阿瑟·戈登通过斐济酋长施行间接统治，把大部分土地保留为不可转让的斐济人财产，并从印度引入契约劳工，由此塑造了延续至1970年独立的“两大族群”社会。

name.zh: 阿瑟·汉密尔顿-戈登爵士
埃弗拉德·伊姆·特恩爵士

sources.title: B. V. Lal, Broken Waves: A History of the Fiji Islands in the Twentieth Century (University of Hawaii Press, 1992)

summary.en: Independent from 10 October 1970 as a dominion, Fiji became a republic after the military coups of 1987. Tension between indigenous Fijians and Indo-Fijians shaped coups in 1987, 2000 and 2006; a new constitution in 2013 introduced common citizenship and elections resumed in 2014.
summary.zh: 斐济于1970年10月10日以自治领身份独立，1987年军事政变后成为共和国。原住民斐济人与印度裔斐济人之间的紧张关系贯穿了1987年、2000年和2006年的政变；2013年新宪法确立共同公民身份，2014年恢复选举。

name.zh: 拉图·卡米塞塞·马拉爵士

sources.title: B. V. Lal, Islands of Turmoil: Elections and Politics in Fiji (ANU Press, 2006)

note: Rulers listed are prime ministers (heads of government).

name.zh: 毛利王运动（基英伊坦加）

summary.en: A movement that united several iwi under a Māori monarch to stop land sales and to stand as an equal beside the British Crown. Centred on Waikato–Tainui, it was invaded by colonial forces in 1863–64 and lost vast lands to confiscation, yet survived as an enduring Māori institution.
summary.zh: 该运动把多个毛利部落团结在一位毛利君主之下，以阻止土地出售，并与英国王室平起平坐。其中心在怀卡托-泰努伊，1863至1864年遭殖民军入侵，大片土地被没收，但作为持久的毛利机构延续至今。

name.en: Nga wai hono i te po

sources.title: Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: Kīngitanga – the Māori King movement

story.en:
By the 1850s settlers outnumbered Māori, and land was passing out of Māori hands faster than many chiefs could accept. Wiremu Tāmihana Tarapīpipi of Ngāti Hauā and others sought a leader of great mana who could unite the tribes. In 1857 the elderly Waikato chief Pōtatau Te Wherowhero agreed, and in June 1858 he was installed as king at Ngāruawāhia.

The government saw the movement as a rival to the Crown. In July 1863 Governor George Grey sent troops across the Mangatāwhiri stream into the Waikato. After Rangiriri and Ōrākau the Kīngitanga withdrew south into what became known as the King Country, and some 1.2 million acres of Waikato land were confiscated.

Tāwhiao kept his people apart for almost two decades before making peace in 1881. In 1995 the Crown apologised to Waikato–Tainui and returned land and money in a settlement signed by Queen Te Atairangikaahu, whose 40-year reign made her the longest-serving Māori monarch.
story.zh:
到19世纪50年代，白人移民人数已超过毛利人，土地流失之快令许多酋长难以接受。恩加蒂豪阿部落的威雷穆·塔米哈纳·塔拉皮皮皮等人四处寻找一位德高望重、能团结各部落的领袖。1857年，年迈的怀卡托酋长波塔陶·特韦罗韦罗应允，1858年6月在恩加鲁阿瓦西亚即位为王。

殖民政府视该运动为王室的对手。1863年7月，总督乔治·格雷派军越过曼加塔菲里溪进入怀卡托。经朗伊里里和奥拉考两役后，毛利王运动退往南方，那里后来被称为“国王之地”，约120万英亩怀卡托土地被没收。

塔菲奥带领族人隔绝自守近二十年，1881年才与政府媾和。1995年，王室向怀卡托-泰努伊正式道歉，并以和解协议归还土地和资金；签署协议的特阿泰朗伊卡阿胡女王在位40年，是在位最久的毛利君主。

summary.en: Britain's first Australian colony, founded as a penal settlement at Sydney Cove in 1788 on the land of the Eora. Ruled by naval and military governors until a legislative council in 1824 and responsible government in 1856, it gave birth to Van Diemen's Land, Victoria, Queensland and New Zealand before joining the federation in 1901.
summary.zh: 英国在澳大利亚的第一个殖民地，1788年作为流放地建立于伊奥拉人土地上的悉尼湾。最初由海军和陆军出身的总督统治，1824年设立立法会，1856年实行责任政府。范迪门地、维多利亚、昆士兰和新西兰都曾由其分出，1901年加入联邦。

summary.en: The federation of six British colonies proclaimed on 1 January 1901. Parliament sat in Melbourne until Canberra opened in 1927. The Commonwealth fought in both world wars, abandoned the White Australia policy in the 1960s–70s and, since the 1967 referendum and the Mabo decision, has slowly reckoned with Indigenous rights.
summary.zh: 1901年1月1日宣告成立的六个英国殖民地的联邦。议会在墨尔本开会，直至1927年堪培拉启用。联邦参加了两次世界大战，在20世纪60至70年代废除“白澳政策”，自1967年公投和马宝案以来逐步正视原住民权利问题。

summary.en: British sovereignty was proclaimed in 1840 after the Treaty of Waitangi; New Zealand became a separate colony in 1841, a self-governing colony with an elected parliament from 1854, a dominion in 1907 and fully independent in law in 1947. It pioneered women's suffrage and a welfare state.
summary.zh: 1840年《怀唐伊条约》签订后，英国宣布对新西兰拥有主权；1841年成为独立殖民地，1854年起设民选议会实行自治，1907年成为自治领，1947年在法律上完全独立。新西兰率先实行妇女选举权并建立福利国家。

summary.en: Formed from the Australian-administered territories of Papua and New Guinea, PNG became independent on 16 September 1975 under Michael Somare. With more than 800 languages it is one of the most culturally diverse nations on earth; the Bougainville conflict of 1988–98 was its gravest crisis.
summary.zh: 巴布亚新几内亚由澳大利亚管理的巴布亚和新几内亚两地合并而成，1975年9月16日在迈克尔·索马雷领导下独立。该国有八百多种语言，是世界上文化最多元的国家之一；1988至1998年的布干维尔冲突是其最严重的危机。

sources.title: J. Griffin, H. Nelson & S. Firth, Papua New Guinea: A Political History (Heinemann, 1979)

summary.en: On 1 January 1962 Western Samoa, a New Zealand-administered UN trust territory, became the first Pacific Island nation to regain independence. Its constitution blends parliamentary democracy with fa'a Sāmoa: until 1990 only matai (chiefs) could vote. It dropped 'Western' from its name in 1997.
summary.zh: 1962年1月1日，由新西兰管理的联合国托管地西萨摩亚成为第一个重获独立的太平洋岛国。其宪法把议会民主与“萨摩亚之道”相结合：1990年以前只有马塔伊（酋长）有投票权。1997年国名去掉“西”字。
